Rashi on Pesachim 112a:11:1.hebrew: לא למיזבן מיניה ולא לזבוני ליה - דאיידי דעדיף מזליה, נצח וזכי ליה להאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 112a:11:1.english: Do not buy from him and do not sell to him - Since his fortune is superior, he will prevail and win out over this [person].

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:12:1.hebrew: אמר ליה ר"ש בן יוחי ומי בסכנה - והלא העגל בסכנה, ומה לך בכך:
Rashi on Pesachim 112a:12:1.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said to him: And who is in danger? - Is not the calf in danger, and what [concern] is it to you?

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:13:1.english: If you wish to strangle yourself - [meaning] to say something that will be heeded by people and [that] they will accept from you.

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:13:2.english: Hang yourself on a tall tree - Say [it] in the name of a great man.

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:13:3.hebrew: בחדתא - כשהתינוק למד בחדש, כשהוא מתחיל ללמוד:
Rashi on Pesachim 112a:13:3.english: With a new [text] - When the child learns something new, when he begins to study.

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:1:1.hebrew: דמסוכר - מקיז דם מן הכתפיים, לשון סיכורי:
Rashi on Pesachim 112a:1:1.english: [One] who lets blood - One who lets blood from the shoulders, [from] the expression sikkurei.

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:1:2.english: Hand on nostrils - [One] who is accustomed to place his hand near his nostrils, upon his lips.

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:1:3.english: A way to fear - It is a way to bring upon him the fear of an evil spirit.

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:4:1.english: Lul, Shafan, Anigron, Anirdafi - It is an incantation.

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:4:2.hebrew: בי בליעי ושמיני - הנה סביבותי אנשים כחושים ושמנים, ותניחוני:
Rashi on Pesachim 112a:4:2.english: Between lean and fat [people] - Behold, around me are lean and fat people, and leave me alone.

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:4:3.english: And he should say to him - "I thirst for water."

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:8:1.english: Be bold - Strengthen yourself in [performing] a mitzvah more than is within your ability.

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:9:1.hebrew: אל תשב בגובהה של עיר ותשנה - מקום שבני העיר עוברים ושבין, שמא כשהן עוברין ושבין יבטלוך ויפסיקוך ממשנתך:
Rashi on Pesachim 112a:9:1.english: Do not sit at the high point of a city and study - [That is,] a place where the townspeople come and go, lest while they are coming and going they distract you and interrupt you from your study.

Rashi on Pesachim 112a:9:2.english: And do not live in a city whose leaders are Torah scholars - For [each one] is preoccupied with his study and not with the affairs of the community.

Tosafot on Pesachim 112a:13:1.hebrew: שבשתא דעל על - תימה, דרבא גופא אית ליה בלא יחפור (ב"ב דף כא.): "שבשתא ממילא נפקא". ויש לומר דהיינו כשלומד קמי דגריס ולא דייק, שיכול להבין מעצמו כשיגדל; אבל כאן דאיירי בספר שאינו מוגה, סומך על ספרו ואינו יוצא מידי טעותו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 112a:13:1.english: Once a mistake enters, it has entered - [This is] astonishing, for Rava himself holds in [the chapter] Lo Yachpor (Bava Batra 21a) [that] "a mistake leaves on its own." And one can say that that refers to when [a student] learns before [a teacher] who recites [the text] and is not precise, for he is able to understand on his own when he grows up; however, here, where [the Gemara] is speaking of an uncorrected book, he relies on his book and does not get free of his mistake.

Tosafot on Pesachim 112a:9:1.hebrew: צוה רבי עקיבא את רבי יהושע בנו - פירש רשב"ם דהוא ר' יהושע בן קרחה, דר"ע קרח היה, כדאמרינן [בבכורות] (דף נח.) שהיה בן עזאי אומר: "כל חכמי ישראל דומין לפני כקליפת השום חוץ מן הקרח הזה". ואין נראה שיהיה הגמרא קורא אותו "בן קרחה" דרך גנאי, שהרי נענשו הנערים שקראו לאלישע "עלה קרח" (מלכים ב ב׳:כ״ג), ובן עזאי קראו כן דרך בדיחותא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 112a:9:1.english: "Rabbi Akiva commanded Rabbi Yehoshua, his son" - Rashbam explained that he is Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah, for Rabbi Akiva was bald, as we say [in Bekhorot] (58a) that Ben Azzai used to say: "All the Sages of Israel are like the peel of garlic before me, except for this bald one." However, it does not appear [plausible] that the Gemara would call him "ben Korchah" in a derogatory manner, for behold, the youths who called out to Elisha, "Go up, baldhead!" (II Kings 2:23) were punished; and Ben Azzai [only] called him so in jest.
